question: A case file was closed four years ago. Its retention period is five years from closure, and an active preservation hold applies to the file. May it be destroyed now, and what should happen when the hold is released?

reference_materials.content: The retention clock begins on the recorded closure date. Destruction may occur only after the full retention period expires, subject to any active hold.

Records subject to an active preservation hold must not be destroyed. A hold suspends destruction, not the underlying retention clock. When the hold is formally released, recalculate eligibility under the applicable retention schedule and destroy records only if the retention period has expired.

synthesis_rationale: The records manual sets a five-year period beginning at closure and makes destruction subject to active holds. The hold procedure independently prohibits destruction during the hold and states that the retention clock continues. Applying both provisions means the file cannot be destroyed now and still has one year left after the hold is released.
